ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-014", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Additional rules: choose the category that the evidence about the cause supports, not the one the symptoms suggest. downstream_timeout needs evidence that the dependency itself is slow or that calls to it timed out. Cite the evidence that identifies the cause (the telltale log line or the metric that changed), not only symptom lines.

Alert: payments-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 05:44 UTC)
Alerting service: payments
Alert time: 2026-08-04T05:44:00Z
Data available from 2026-08-04T04:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T07:00:00Z

Evidence:
Step 1: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-08-04T06:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-08-04T05:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate evolution around the alert time for payments service)
  Result: M-041: Change detected at 2026-08-04T05:40:00Z: mean 0.41 before, 22.16 after (264.8 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-041] payments.error_rate_pct from 2026-08-04T05:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.28 max=22.26 mean=8.78 last=22.03; mean=8.78. Change detected at 2026-08-04T05:40:00Z: mean 0.41 before, 22.16 after (264.8 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-08-04T05:10:00Z = 0.28 (lowest); 2026-08-04T05:40:00Z = 22.16 (first point after the change); 2026-08-04T05:45:00Z = 22.26 (peak); 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z = 22.03 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-08-04T06:00:00Z", "metric": "cpu_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-08-04T05:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check CPU usage for payments service)
  Result: M-038: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-038] payments.cpu_pct from 2026-08-04T05:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=30.11 max=43.27 mean=38.91 last=39.69; mean=38.91. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-08-04T05:15:00Z = 30.11 (lowest); 2026-08-04T05:40:00Z = 43.27 (peak); 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z = 39.69 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-08-04T05:45:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "error,warn,fail,cert,exception", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-08-04T05:30:00Z"} (asked because: Search logs for any errors, warnings or cert issues in payments service)
  Result: 4 matching log lines.
  [L-0279] 2026-08-04T05:40:11Z payments ERROR request failed status=502 path=/api/v1/stock request_id=req-8d5e3882
  [L-0280] 2026-08-04T05:40:16Z payments ERROR request failed status=500 path=/api/v1/stock request_id=req-a93172eb duration_ms=16318
  [L-0294] 2026-08-04T05:43:25Z payments WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0297] 2026-08-04T05:44:05Z payments ERROR request failed status=502 path=/api/v1/stock request_id=req-eea911b7
Step 4: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-08-04T06:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-08-04T05:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check inventory service error rate to see if the dependency is failing)
  Result: M-023: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-023] inventory.error_rate_pct from 2026-08-04T05:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.14 max=0.64 mean=0.37 last=0.3; mean=0.37. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-08-04T05:25:00Z = 0.64 (peak); 2026-08-04T05:35:00Z = 0.14 (lowest); 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z = 0.3 (last).
Step 5: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-08-04T06:00:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-08-04T05:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check inventory service latency to see if it is timing out)
  Result: M-024: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-024] inventory.latency_p99_ms from 2026-08-04T05:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=104.9 max=131.29 mean=119.32 last=104.9; mean=119.32. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-08-04T05:50:00Z = 131.29 (peak); 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z = 104.9 (last); 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z = 104.9 (lowest).
Step 6: runbook_retrieve {"query": "how to mitigate and fix bad deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)"} (asked because: Retrieve mitigation guidance before diagnosing.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-01-3 (similarity 0.65).
  [R-01-3] Bad deployment or regression - How to confirm (similarity 0.65): Line the start of the trouble up against the release timeline. If it began just after a rollout and the previous version was healthy, suspect the release. Look at what the service wrote to its logs while the new version was starting and when the first failures arrived, and compare with an older instance if one is still running.
  [R-01-5] Bad deployment or regression - Mitigation (similarity 0.63): Go back to the previous release straight away by redeploying the last version known to be good. Do not spend time debugging on the live service first. Pause any further releases to this service until the cause is understood and a fix has been reviewed and tested.
  [R-01-1] Bad deployment or regression - Summary (similarity 0.62): A new version of a service went out and something in it does not work. This is the most common reason for a sudden, lasting rise in failures, and it is usually fixed fastest by undoing the change rather than by investigating on the live system.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- bad_deployment: The error rate jumped abruptly starting precisely at 05:40 UTC without CPU anomalies or dependency degradation, pointing towards a recent bad deployment or configuration change. (evidence: M-041, L-0279, L-0280)
- misconfiguration: Sudden HTTP 502 and 500 errors starting at a precise timestamp could indicate an invalid environment variable or upstream routing misconfiguration. (evidence: M-041, L-0279, L-0297)
- downstream_timeout: Although inventory service metrics appear healthy, other downstream services or databases called by payments-service may be timing out or failing. (evidence: L-0280, L-0297)
